# Android releases

Android builds use the selected production backend and channel. Without signing credentials the release APK uses the default debug key; it is installable but is not Play-ready. This key can change between runners, so replacing an installed app may require uninstalling it and losing local data. The manifest records the signing mode and certificate identity to prevent reuse across signing changes.

Configure either `DISPOSABL_ANDROID_SIGNING` or all four `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` and `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` secrets to produce a signed APK and AAB. Incomplete or invalid signing fails the build. Expo remains required for this pipeline's update integration.

Production inputs reject E2E configuration and require non-loopback HTTPS backend URLs. APKs and signed bundles are checked against the selected Expo configuration. A signed AAB also passes the pinned bundletool's structure, manifest, ABI and target SDK checks before it is retained. The fallback APK does not require bundletool or Play credentials. These checks do not establish Play account readiness or prove device behavior.

Play submission is separate and defaults off. Set `ANDROID_PLAY_SUBMIT` to `true`, select `ANDROID_PLAY_TRACK`, set `ANDROID_PLAY_UPLOAD_CERT_SHA256` to the lowercase SHA-256 of the upload certificate, and provide `ANDROID_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` as a service-account JSON secret. Expo project and token are also required. This is an operator assertion that the Play app and access are configured; submission errors remain failures. Play account setup or a manual first upload may still be required, and submission does not mean review or rollout succeeded.

The Disposabl product uses the same artifact build, with EAS Update enabled for its production project and channel. Its Play submission checks the product package and the reset upload certificate verified in Play on November 16, 2026 (SHA-1 `9E:8B:A8:A6:CC:91:07:8A:46:4F:BE:F2:52:86:0B:C8:FE:FB:18:B2`, SHA-256 `92ad2c5b65aad964b622a4b4fede94b40a31dcae0eb537b9201ea464689a9fb9`). The upload-key check gates submission, not artifact builds. Android version codes use `1000 + 100 * run number + attempt`; verify the candidate exceeds the latest Play version before submission.

Queued Disposabl Android releases may finish after another push to main, provided their immutable event commit remains an ancestor of main. Rewritten history, mismatched checkouts and failed source lookups are rejected. PR previews and generated apps retain their current-head checks. Product builds require analytics and payments enabled and both arm64-v8a and x86_64. Production configuration requires the Disposabl Expo project, production channel, and fingerprint runtime; the AAB's native update metadata is verified as well.

Product main pushes currently build a new native artifact rather than automatically publishing an update. For a controlled JavaScript-only update, first compare its Android fingerprint with the verified installed production build and confirm the source and production public environment match the intended release. Publish to the production channel with the EAS CLI only when the fingerprints match; native changes require a new store build. Verify the update on an installed production build and after relaunch. Older builds created with OTA disabled cannot receive updates and must be replaced through the store.
